Hi Alex — great to meet you and the team today, thanks for the time and the detailed walkthrough of your use case. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can get you a clean cost estimate:

1) Recap of what we heard:
- ~15k monthly active users, peak concurrency expected ~200 requests/min.
- Typical request = user prompt (~150–300 characters) + system prompt + model reply (~600–1,200 characters).
- Workload: mix of short summaries and multi-turn chat for care coordination.

2) What we need from you (helpful to finalize pricing ballpark):
- Typical daily/monthly request volume (or sample CSV).
- Desired budget range / target $/1M tokens (you mentioned wanting to keep unit economics near $10–30 per 1M tokens).
- Any mandatory SLA or on-prem constraints.

3) Important note on metrics (quick primer because we saw some confusion on the call):
- Tokens vs characters vs requests: billed usage is measured in tokens (approx 4 characters = 1 token for English, but it varies). Requests is simply API calls. Characters are not a billing unit but can be used to estimate tokens.
- Prompt caching: If you enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, you will see fewer billed tokens on subsequent requests for the same prompt prefix — but the billing still counts tokens consumed by the response + any uncached prompt portion.

Attached I included a simple example calc that maps characters -> estimated tokens -> cost for several scenarios (pricing-example-1Mcalc.xlsx) and a sample CSV layout for usage (acme-usage-snapshot.csv).

Next steps: if you can drop a week of representative request counts or confirm an expected monthly request count range, I'll run 3 unit-economics scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic) and loop in Nikhil (SE) and Rishi (AE) for a quick follow-up call.

Thanks — great questions, Alex. Below are plain-language answers plus a worked example.

1) Tokens vs characters: use chars -> tokens as a budget approximation (4 chars ≈ 1 token) for English text. However, variability exists (e.g., code, punctuation, non-Latin scripts). For budgeting, converting historical character counts using the 4:1 ratio is acceptable; for final contractual sizing we recommend sampling ~1–2k representative requests and running an exact tokenization pass.

2) Prompt caching behavior:
- First request that sends the full prompt (prefix + variable) will be billed for all tokens in that request.
- Subsequent requests that reuse the cached prefix will only be billed for the uncached tokens (commonly the variable prompt + the model response).
- Caching is most effective when you have a stable system prompt or patient metadata that repeats across requests.

3) Requests vs billed tokens mapping:
- The simplest conversion is: monthly_billed_tokens = sum_over_requests(estimated_tokens_per_request). If you only have # requests, multiply by an average tokens/request (use conservative and optimistic averages).
- Example (attached spreadsheet uses these numbers):
  - Avg prompt chars: 800 chars => ~200 tokens input
  - Avg response chars: 1,200 chars => ~300 tokens output
  - Billed tokens/request ≈ 500 tokens
  - If you have 100k requests/month => 50M tokens/month => at $20 / 1M tokens => ~$1,000/month.

Worked scenarios (high-level):
- Optimistic: 250 tokens/request => 1M requests => 250M tokens => at $12 / 1M => $3,000/month
- Expected: 500 tokens/request => 200k requests => 100M tokens => at $20 / 1M => $2,000/month
- Conservative: 800 tokens/request => 100k requests => 80M tokens => at $30 / 1M => $2,400/month

I attached the same calc and a sample tokenization script link in the Doc (https://docs.redwood.ai/pricing-metrics-reference) — if you can share a week of logs (anonymized) that would be perfect. Our SE (Nikhil) can run the conversion and produce an expected tokens/month CSV.

Also: for procurement comparisons, we can provide a normalized row: "cost per 1M billed tokens" and "cost per 1k requests (assuming X avg tokens/request)" so you can feed both figures into your vendor evaluation spreadsheet.

If it's helpful, I'm free for a 30m sync tomorrow morning — otherwise send the sample logs and we'll run the numbers.
